statement: Guth–Maynard's density upper bound alone does not verify BGSTB's strong-density premise. At sigma=3/4 it gives exponent5/9; premise asks o(T^{1/2}).
compatible_assumptions: Fixed sigma3/4 lies in required BGSTB range; two-sided vs positive heights changes only constant, irrelevant to exponent.
already_proved: Original bounds as stated, exact exponent arithmetic.
conjectural: Actual strong density may hold; no refutation implied.
next_step: Prove o(T^{2(1-sigma)}) with required uniformity in moving endpoint range, or bypass that premise as Lamzouri's finite inequality does.
counterexample_to_inference: Numerical growth model M(T)=T^{19/36} satisfies an O(T^{5/9}) bound but is not o(T^{1/2}); this is a logical growth witness, not a zero distribution.
significance: Prevents erroneous theorem chaining; identifies a real exponent/quantifier gap.
difficulty: high for stronger analytic theorem; arithmetic check elementary

kind: established source connection, not new discovery
statement: Fixed-test unconditional weighted pair correlation combines with conjugation-symmetric tensor positivity after differential deweighting Q-Q''/(4log^2T).
compatible_assumptions: eta smooth real even supported strictly inside(-1/2,1/2), integral eta^2=1; Q=eta^2*eta^2 and Q'' fixed, smooth, supported[-1,1]; zero multiset conjugation invariant.
already_proved: Lamzouri states and proves this in section3; local Fourier algebra checked here.
conjectural: Effective finite-T bound with completely explicit constants not derived here.
next_step: Extract effective dependence on Q and Q'' from BGSTB proof, keep smoothing fixed before T-limit.
potential_counterexamples: Dropping conjugation symmetry fails already at Z={i}; varying tests without uniform error control invalidates inference.
tests: Random finite multiset stress tests are nonrigorous supplements only.
significance: Reusable way to replace termwise positivity by a global Hilbert-space norm.
difficulty: moderate effective reconstruction, substantial analytic bookkeeping

statement: At the density-envelope bottleneck sigma7/10, improved S3 control must confront near-extremal sets with |W|~T1^{2/3}, energy~|W|^{5/2}, and R(v)=sum_W |v|^{it} concentrated near rationals of scale T1^{1/3}.
already_proved: Authors identify this obstruction; S1/S2 tight within their framework.
conjectural: An incidence-theoretic or rational-concentration inverse theorem can yield a power saving for all relevant W.
next_step: Reconstruct Proposition9.1 sharpness configuration, quantify exclusion needed for S3 saving, then test against clustered arithmetic/rational models.
potential_counterexamples: Generic-random-set gains do not cover worst-case large-value sets.
significance: Targets exact loss instead of vague transplant rhetoric.
status: source-backed research target; no new bound proved
